```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center", dpi = 96)
suppressMessages({ library(data.table); library(ggplot2); library(patchwork); library(knitr); library(FNN) })
ROOT <- if (dir.exists("data")) "." else ".."
d <- fread(file.path(ROOT, "data", "mc903_cells.csv.gz"))
ORDER <- c("WT_Ear","WT_Neck","WT_Flank","d0_WT_neck","d3_MC903_neck","d6_MC903_neck","d9_MC903_Ear","d9_MC903_Neck","d9_MC903_Flank",
           "d12_MC903_neck","d10_OXA_Ear","d10_OXA_Neck","d10_OXA_Flank","d16_OXA_Ear","d16_OXA_Neck","d16_OXA_Flank")
d[, sample := factor(sample, levels = ORDER)]; d[, site := tolower(site)]
d[, class := fcase(grepl("^KC", celltype_broad), "Keratinocyte", grepl("^HF|^SG", celltype_broad), "Hair follicle / sebaceous",
                   grepl("^FIB", celltype_broad), "Fibroblast", celltype_broad == "Adipocyte", "Adipocyte", celltype_broad == "Chondrocyte", "Cartilage",
                   celltype_broad %in% c("SM","Pericyte","VEC","LEC","Schwann","MEL"), "Vessel / muscle / nerve", default = "Immune")]

# Layer labels: defined once in code/skin_layers.R (depth compartments = system A; neighbourhood naming/collapse = system B).
# The logic and the reasons for every cut are documented there.
source(file.path(ROOT, "code", "skin_layers.R"))
d <- assign_skin_layers(d); B <- attr(d, "bounds")[order(match(sample, ORDER))]; CC <- SKIN_CC
d[, sample := factor(sample, levels = ORDER)]

# palettes for populations
PAL_CLASS <- c("Keratinocyte" = "#d62728", "Hair follicle / sebaceous" = "#ff7f0e", "Fibroblast" = "#1f77b4", "Adipocyte" = "#f7e300",
               "Cartilage" = "#7f7f7f", "Vessel / muscle / nerve" = "#9467bd", "Immune" = "#2ca02c")
PAL_FIB <- c("KC (reference)" = "grey85", FIB = "#9ecae1", FIB_Papillary = "#e41a1c", FIB_Reticular = "#377eb8", FIB_Subcutis = "#f7e300",
             FIB_Subfascia = "#984ea3", FIB_DS = "#ff7f00", FIB_DP = "#a65628", FIB_Cycling = "#999999", FIB_ProInf = "#000000")
PAL_KC <- c("KC_IFE" = "#1f77b4", "KC_Stressed_Basal" = "#ff7f0e", "KC_Stressed_Cycling" = "#2ca02c", "KC_Stressed_Diff" = "#d62728",
            "HF / sebaceous" = "grey80", "other (reference)" = "grey95")
IMM <- c("MAC","DC","Neutrophil","Mast","Basophil","LC","NK","ILC2","TC_gdt","TC_Treg","TC_Th17","TC_Cd4","TC_Cd8","TC_Cyc","Lymphocyte")
PAL_IMM <- setNames(c("#1f77b4","#aec7e8","#2ca02c","#ff7f0e","#000000","#8c564b","#e377c2","#bcbd22","#17becf","#9467bd","#d62728","#ff9896","#c49c94","#7f7f7f","#dbdb8d"), IMM)

# rotate every strip so its long axis is horizontal and the epidermis is at the TOP
rot <- function(x) {
  pc <- prcomp(cbind(x$x, x$y))$rotation; u <- cbind(x$x, x$y) %*% pc
  k <- x$class == "Keratinocyte"; if (sum(k) > 20 && median(u[k, 2]) < median(u[!k, 2])) u[, 2] <- -u[, 2]
  x[, `:=`(u = u[, 1] - min(u[, 1]), v = u[, 2] - min(u[, 2]))]; x
}
d <- rbindlist(lapply(split(d, d$sample), rot)); d[, sample := factor(sample, levels = ORDER)]
d[, c("length_mm", "thick_mm") := .(round(diff(range(u)) / 1000, 1), round(diff(range(v)) / 1000, 1)), by = sample]

base <- function(x, pt) ggplot(x, aes(u, v)) + geom_point(size = pt) + coord_equal(expand = FALSE) + theme_bw(8) +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(), legend.key.size = unit(.35, "cm"), legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.title = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 9)) + guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2.5), ncol = 1))
p_depth <- function(x, pt) { x <- copy(x)[, L := ifelse(celltype == "Chondrocyte", "CART (ref)", as.character(layer_depth))]
  base(x[order(L == "CART (ref)")], pt) + aes(colour = L) + scale_colour_manual(values = PAL5, drop = FALSE) + ggtitle("depth compartments (label-blind): EPI | PAP upper 40% of dermis | RET to fat onset | SUB | SUBFAS below panniculus") }
p_nn3   <- function(x, pt) base(x, pt) + aes(colour = layer_nn) + scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_NN3, drop = FALSE) + ggtitle("authors' neighbourhood collapsed to layers (composition-derived)")
p_nn    <- function(x, pt) base(x, pt) + aes(colour = name) + scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_NN, drop = FALSE) + ggtitle("authors' neighbourhood clusters (CellCharter k = 11), named")
p_class <- function(x, pt) base(x[order(class == "Immune")], pt) + aes(colour = class) + scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_CLASS, drop = FALSE) + ggtitle("broad cell class")
p_fib   <- function(x, pt) { x <- copy(x)[, f := ifelse(grepl("^FIB", celltype), celltype, ifelse(class == "Keratinocyte", "KC (reference)", NA))][!is.na(f)]
  base(x[order(f != "KC (reference)", f == "FIB_ProInf")], pt) + aes(colour = f) + scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_FIB, drop = FALSE) + ggtitle("fibroblast subtypes (pro-inflammatory = black)") }
p_kc    <- function(x, pt) { x <- copy(x)[, k := fcase(celltype %in% names(PAL_KC), celltype, grepl("^HF|^SG", celltype_broad), "HF / sebaceous", default = "other (reference)")]
  base(x[order(k %in% c("other (reference)", "HF / sebaceous"), decreasing = TRUE)], pt) + aes(colour = k) + scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_KC, drop = FALSE) + ggtitle("keratinocyte states") }
p_imm   <- function(x, pt) { x <- copy(x)[, i := ifelse(celltype %in% IMM, celltype, ifelse(class == "Keratinocyte", "KC (reference)", NA))][!is.na(i)]
  base(x[order(i != "KC (reference)")], pt) + aes(colour = i) + scale_colour_manual(values = c(PAL_IMM, "KC (reference)" = "grey85"), drop = FALSE) + ggtitle("immune populations") }
window <- function(x, width_um = 2500) { c0 <- median(x$u); x[abs(u - c0) < width_um / 2] }
pct <- function(dt, row, col) dcast(dt[, .N, by = c(row, col)][, p := round(100 * N / sum(N)), by = row], as.formula(paste(row, "~", col)), value.var = "p", fill = 0)
```

# 1. What the data contain

One Seurat object from Mendeley (doi 10.17632/s3hgv4fp7c.1): 404,283 MERFISH cells (plus 27,571 scRNA-seq cells, dropped here), 500-gene panel,
FFPE, 3 MERSCOPE runs. Per-cell table exported to `data/mc903_cells.csv.gz`:

| column | what it is | levels |
|---|---|---|
| `cell` | cell id (run date + Baysor entity id) | 404,283 |
| `sample` | tissue strip; one section per condition x site | 16 |
| `timepoint`, `condition`, `site` | Untreated / MC903 d3 d6 d9 d12 / OXA d10 d16; WT / MC903 / OXA; ear, neck, flank | 7 / 3 / 3 |
| `rundate` | MERSCOPE run (slide); strips on one run share a coordinate frame | 3 |
| `x`, `y` | cell centroid, micrometres, slide frame | |
| `celltype_broad`, `celltype` | authors' annotation; fine level has FIB_Papillary / Reticular / Subcutis / Subfascia / ProInf and KC_IFE / KC_Stressed_* | 26 / 42 |
| `cc11` | authors' CellCharter neighbourhood cluster (k = 11) | 11 |
| `n_counts`, `n_genes`, `volume` | per-cell QC | |

**There is no anatomical layer label.** The paper describes papillary dermis, reticular dermis, subcutis and subfascia (Fig. 2G) but only as fibroblast
subtypes, not as a region label on every cell. The neighbourhood cluster is the only region-like label and it is derived from the cell types around
each cell. So two layer systems are built below: **A. depth compartments** (what the method uses) and **B. the neighbourhood collapse** (the authors'
labels, as a comparator, built the way MU/SM/ME were built in the colon). Mouse id is also absent: one section per strip.

# 2. The 16 strips

```{r samples}
tab <- d[, .(cells = .N, length_mm = length_mm[1], thickness_mm = thick_mm[1], fibroblasts = sum(class == "Fibroblast"),
             papillary = sum(celltype == "FIB_Papillary"), reticular = sum(celltype == "FIB_Reticular"), pro_inflam = sum(celltype == "FIB_ProInf"),
             KC_IFE = sum(celltype == "KC_IFE"), KC_stressed = sum(grepl("^KC_Stressed", celltype))), by = .(sample, condition, timepoint, site, rundate)][order(sample)]
kable(tab, caption = "One section per strip. Length / thickness: extents of the rotated strip (epidermis along the top edge).")
```

# 3. Layer system A: depth compartments (label-blind)

**Rule.** depth = distance from the nearest keratinocyte of the connected epidermal sheet in the same strip (the sheet is the surface anchor, as the
lumen is in the colon; keratinocytes within 40 um of each other are linked and only components of >= 300 cells count, which drops hair-follicle bulbs
that carry keratinocyte labels deep in the tissue). EPI: depth <= 10 um. PAP: the upper 40% of the dermis, i.e. 10 um to 0.4 x fat onset. RET: the lower 60%, down to the fat onset.
SUB: fat onset to the panniculus carnosus. SUBFAS: below the panniculus. Fat onset = 10th percentile of adipocyte depth per strip (dermal white
adipose tissue); panniculus = median depth of the strip's muscle cells. Fat and muscle are landmarks, not populations under test. The papillary cut is
relative rather than a fixed micrometre value because mouse dermis is only 120-190 um thick (a human 100 um cut would swallow the reticular dermis) and
because the dermis thickens with oedema; 0.4 is a histological convention, not fitted to the fibroblast labels (normal papillary median depth 34 um,
reticular 70 um; sensitivity at 0.3 / 0.5 to follow). Ear cartilage is overlaid in grey: it splits the ear into two faces, so ear depths beyond ~100 um are not comparable.

```{r bounds}
cnt <- dcast(d[, .N, by = .(sample, layer_depth)], sample ~ layer_depth, value.var = "N", fill = 0)
kable(merge(B, cnt, by = "sample")[order(sample)], caption = "Per-strip boundaries (um) and cells per compartment. b_fas = Inf: no panniculus captured, so no subfascia. Ear strips: cartilage in the middle, deep compartments unreliable.")
```

```{r depth_density, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 5.5}
fd <- d[celltype %in% c("FIB_Papillary", "FIB_Reticular", "FIB_Subcutis", "FIB_Subfascia", "FIB_ProInf") & depth < 600 & site != "ear"]
fd[, condition := factor(condition, levels = c("WT", "MC903", "OXA"))]
ggplot(fd, aes(depth, colour = celltype)) + geom_density(adjust = 1.2, linewidth = .8) + facet_wrap(~ condition, nrow = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(10, PAP_FRAC * median(B$b_sub), median(B$b_sub)), linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") + scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_FIB) + theme_bw(10) +
  labs(x = "depth from keratinocyte edge (um); dashed = EPI/PAP, PAP/RET and RET/SUB cuts at the median strip", y = "density", colour = NULL,
       title = "Fibroblast subtypes along depth (neck + flank). Normal: papillary < reticular < subcutis < subfascia. Disease: pro-inflammatory fibroblasts fill the papillary/upper reticular band")
```

# 4. Layer system B: the authors' neighbourhood clusters, and how they were named

**Logic of the labels.** Each CellCharter cluster was named from four things: its cell-type composition (table below, top three types), its median
depth from the keratinocyte edge, whether it exists in normal skin (NN) or appears with disease (IAN), and the paper's own description (NN1 epidermis,
NN2 upper pilosebaceous unit, NN3 dermis, NN4 subcutis, NN5 ear cartilage; IAN1-6 inflammation-associated). The collapse to EPI / DER / SUB / CART then
follows depth, exactly as MU1-11 -> MU in the colon. Two of the paper's names are misleading on the data: cluster 0 ("upper dermis") sits at the
dermo-epidermal junction (median depth 11 um), and cluster 10 ("deep") sits at 88 um, the same depth as the other inflamed-dermis cluster.

```{r cc_table}
comp <- d[, .N, by = .(cc11, celltype_broad)][, p := round(100 * N / sum(N)), by = cc11][order(cc11, -p)][, head(.SD, 3), by = cc11][, .(composition = paste0(celltype_broad, " ", p, "%", collapse = ", ")), by = cc11]
dep  <- d[, .(median_depth_um = round(median(depth, na.rm = TRUE)), pct_normal = round(100 * mean(condition == "WT"), 1)), by = cc11]
prev <- dcast(d[, .N, by = .(cc11, condition)][, p := round(100 * N / sum(N)), by = condition], cc11 ~ condition, value.var = "p", fill = 0)
setnames(prev, c("WT", "MC903", "OXA"), c("pct_of_normal_cells", "pct_of_MC903_cells", "pct_of_OXA_cells"))
cct <- Reduce(function(a, b) merge(a, b, by = "cc11"), list(CC, comp, dep[, .(cc11, median_depth_um)], prev))[match(CC$cc11, cc11)]
kable(cct[, .(cc11, name, layer_nn, composition, median_depth_um, pct_of_normal_cells, pct_of_MC903_cells, pct_of_OXA_cells, reading)],
      caption = "Cluster -> name -> collapsed layer, with the evidence used (composition, depth, prevalence) and the biological reading.")
```

The clusters are **states, not places**: cluster 1 (normal epidermis) is replaced by cluster 9 (stressed epidermis), cluster 4 (normal dermis) by
clusters 2 and 10 (inflamed dermis). These are the skin counterparts of MU1-3 -> MU4/MU6-8 in the DSS colon, and they are what the method's
output should be checked against, not an input it conditions on.

# 5. Why the method uses system A

```{r compare}
k1 <- pct(d[condition == "WT" & celltype %in% c("FIB_Papillary", "FIB_Reticular", "FIB_Subcutis", "FIB_Subfascia") & site != "ear"], "celltype", "layer_depth")
k2 <- pct(d[condition != "WT" & celltype == "FIB_ProInf" & site != "ear"], "celltype", "layer_depth")
kable(rbind(k1, k2, fill = TRUE), caption = "A. Depth compartments: % of each fibroblast population (normal subtypes; pro-inflammatory in disease), neck + flank")
k3 <- pct(d[condition == "WT" & celltype %in% c("FIB_Papillary", "FIB_Reticular", "FIB_Subcutis", "FIB_Subfascia") & site != "ear"], "celltype", "layer_nn")
k4 <- pct(d[condition != "WT" & celltype == "FIB_ProInf" & site != "ear"], "celltype", "layer_nn")
kable(rbind(k3, k4, fill = TRUE), caption = "B. Neighbourhood collapse: the same populations")
```

```{r leak, fig.width = 16, fig.height = 11}
# Figure: the same composition-derived labelling applied to colon and skin, measured against the anatomy (depth from the epithelial sheet).
source(file.path(ROOT, "code", "leak_figure.R"))
colon_csv <- file.path(ROOT, "..", "all_slices", "062921_D0_m3a_1_slice_1.csv")
if (file.exists(colon_csv)) { pl <- leak_figure(d, colon_csv); print(pl); ggsave(file.path(ROOT, "output", "leak_figure.png"), pl, width = 16, height = 11, dpi = 110) } else cat("colon slice not found:", colon_csv)
```

**Reading the figure.** In the colon the neighbourhood prefixes MU / SM / ME were also composition-derived, but the mucosa is the crypt-bearing zone:
every lamina-propria cell is within a few micrometres of crypt epithelium, the submucosa begins where the crypts end, and the muscularis externa lies
beyond. The composition window therefore switches labels exactly where the histology switches, Fibro 2 falls inside MU and Fibro 7 beyond it, and
the leak into the layer term is harmless. In the skin the equivalent boundary is the dermo-epidermal junction, but the 40-cell window around a cell
just below it is still dominated by keratinocytes, so the "epidermis" neighbourhood extends tens of micrometres into the dermis and covers the papillary
fibroblast peak. The label follows the composition, not the junction, and papillary versus reticular is not resolved at all.

Under the depth compartments papillary fibroblasts are dermal (PAP) and pro-inflammatory fibroblasts occupy PAP/RET, the band the paper says they
arise in. Under the neighbourhood collapse most papillary fibroblasts are called "epidermis" because the 40-cell composition window around them is
keratinocyte-dominated, while pro-inflammatory fibroblasts are "dermis": a layer-overlap term built on system B would penalise the true
papillary -> pro-inflammatory pair. System B also cannot separate papillary from reticular at all. This is the information-leakage argument in
one table: layers must come from anatomy, and the neighbourhood labels belong on the output side as ground truth for the state transitions.

# 7. Each strip {.tabset}

Strips rotated so the epidermis runs along the top edge. First the whole strip by depth compartment (subsampled to 25,000 cells); then a 2.5 mm
central window, all cells: depth compartments vs neighbourhood collapse, neighbourhood clusters vs broad class, fibroblast subtypes vs keratinocyte
states, immune populations.

```{r strips, results = "asis", fig.width = 15, fig.height = 4.2}
for (s in ORDER) {
  x <- d[sample == s]; b <- B[sample == s]
  cat(sprintf("\n\n## %s {.tabset}\n\n%s, %s, %d cells, %.1f x %.1f mm. Fat onset %d um; panniculus %s.\n\n", s, x$timepoint[1], x$site[1], nrow(x),
              x$length_mm[1], x$thick_mm[1], b$b_sub, if (is.finite(b$b_fas)) paste(b$b_fas, "um") else "not captured"))
  set.seed(1); xs <- if (nrow(x) > 25000) x[sort(sample(.N, 25000))] else x
  print(p_depth(xs, .25) + ggtitle(paste(s, "- whole strip, depth compartments")))
  w <- window(x)
  cat("\n\n**Central 2.5 mm window, all cells**\n\n")
  print(p_depth(w, .6) | p_nn3(w, .6))
  print(p_nn(w, .6) | p_class(w, .6))
  print(p_fib(w, .7) | p_kc(w, .6))
  print(p_imm(w, .7) | plot_spacer())
}
```

# 8. Reading guide

* **Normal strips**: EPI (red) along the top, PAP (orange) the upper 40% of the dermis with the papillary fibroblasts, RET (blue) with reticular
  fibroblasts and the pilosebaceous units, SUB (yellow) from the first fat, SUBFAS (purple) below the panniculus where it was captured. The neighbourhood
  collapse gives only EPI / DER / SUB and puts the papillary band into EPI.
* **MC903 d3 -> d6 -> d9 -> d12**: epidermis becomes stressed keratinocytes, papillary fibroblasts disappear and PAP/RET fill with pro-inflammatory
  fibroblasts (black) and macrophage/DC-rich inflamed dermis; neutrophil state and anagen follicles appear with oxazolone. The band thickens with
  oedema (OXA d16 ear 5.4 mm), so depth should be normalised within each strip before comparing sections, as in the kidney.
* **What to feed the method**: `layer_depth` as the layer, depth (or a MorphoGAM curve along the epidermis) as the within-layer coordinate,
  `celltype` as the population; `cc11` / `layer_nn` only as the authors'-label comparator and as ground truth for the state transitions.
